messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] reserved-resv-pool-1: GPU utilization 100% for 6m, queue depth spike 320 -> paging oncall.

oncall-jamie: paging... I'm on it. seeing high qdepth on reserved-resv-pool-1, latency > 2s. @kevin.t @alina.p

kevin.t: looking. Autoscaler attempted scale at 12:34:10 but failed - cloud API 429. logs:
```json
{"attempt":3,"error":"RateLimitExceeded","region":"us-west-2"}
```

alina.p: noisy tenant suspected, tenant_id=enterprise-velvetpay has bursty jobs that pin all GPUs. Can we throttle? @sara.k

sara.k: can confirm reruns from velvetpay correlate with kernel busy. metrics: p99 latency 3.2s, queue_len per-pool:
```text
reserved-resv-pool-1: 320
shared-pool: 12
```

miguel.r: suggestions: 1) enable soft-eviction for batch jobs 2) temporarily reduce velvetpay concurrency via reservation throttles 3) request burst capacity from Dedicated burst queue. Will try 1.

oncall-jamie: executing soft-evict script now
```bash
./scripts/evict-noisy.sh --pool reserved-resv-pool-1 --tenant velvetpay --dry-run
```

oncall-jamie: dry-run shows ~18 pods would be evicted. running with --force

incident-bot: action_log: evict 18 pods from velvetpay at 12:42:01

kevin.t: autoscaler still failing to add nodes due to cloud API rate limit; opened a support ticket, switching to fallback: enable burst-queue with pre-warmed instances. calling infra.

infra-alert: (ops-bot) manual allocation request submitted to cloud: 4 gpus pre-warm us-west-2 (request id x-99234)

alina.p: also toggled per-tenant concurrency limit in routing layer: velvetpay -> 20 concurrent requests

velvetpay-eng: @account-dan I see throttling, is this expected? (message from customer)

sara.k: @account-dan please ack, we're mitigating; will update within 15m. add to incident timeline.

oncall-jamie: queue depth dropped to 70 after evictions and throttle. p95 latency back to 0.9s. still watching. last autoscaler attempt 12:46:18.

kevin.t: cloud support responded: rate limiting will persist for ~10m, recommending staggered retries. We'll hold on autoscale bursts and rely on eviction+throttles for now. Filed follow-up to make autoscaler backoff smarter.

miguel.r: starting a short-term routing fallback: reroute new velvetpay inference traffic to a compatible hosted model (lower-cost) to reduce GPU load. patching route now.

oncall-jamie: applied route switch, new requests routed. monitoring.

incident-bot: metrics snapshot at 12:53:00: reserved-resv-pool-1 utilization 72%, queue-depth 24, p95 latency 0.8s

account-dan: velvetpay confirms decreased error rates, thanks. However asks for postmortem and SLA hit calc.

sara.k: noted. assigning postmortem owner @miguel.r and SLA calc to @alina.p. Creating incident doc.

miguel.r: will capture timeline, root cause looks like combined autoscaler backoff/Cloud rate limits + noisy tenant churn. action items: 1) autoscaler backoff improvements 2) tenant-level admission control defaults 3) reserve burst contract with cloud 4) telemetry for per-tenant GPU usage.

oncall-jamie: adding runbook step to prefer eviction+throttle before autoscale when cloud rate limits present.

ops-bot: created incident-2819994321 in incidents tracker, severity=sev2

sara.k: anything else? we should notify legal/compliance for enterprise impact? Account notified.

kevin.t: log snippets for postmortem:
```text
12:34:10 autoscaler attempt id:a1 -> 429 RateLimitExceeded
12:42:01 evicted 18 pods velvetpay
12:44:30 toggled tenant throttle to 20
12:49:00 route switch to hosted-compat-model
```

alina.p: marking follow-ups: autoscaler fix (owner: infra), tenant admission control (owner: platform), burst capacity pre-warm (owner: sales/ops), customer comms (owner: account).

oncall-jamie: closing paging for now, will remain in thread for 1hr watch. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident closed by oncall-jamie at 13:05:12 (watch mode)
